The cheapest way you can buy small amounts of silver is to buy junk silver coins.

These are worn, used 90% silver US coins that were made pre-1965. Specifically dimes, quarters, and half dollars are easy to get, common, and cheap.

If you have a local coin shop, stop in and ask to see their junk silver. They usually will have a shoe box full of old worn coins that do not have any collectible value.

For a guide to how much you should be paying, see http://www.coinflation.com/silver_coin_values.html

Remember that you are not paying for a collectible coin. You are paying for the amount of silver if you melted down that old quarter.

Right now, the melt values are something like:

Dimes $1.19

Quarters $2.97

Half Dollars $5.95

Don't pay too much. All shops will have a markup above the pure melt value of silver, but should not be too high. Don't be afraid to shop around a little. If you look on ebay, you can see the insanity of people who pay too much for junk.
